reading.body:
The most reusable finding from this set is that every resource here is free to access, and four of the five permit reuse with minimal restriction, making this one of the lower-friction corners of ML education infrastructure.

The five items divide into two practical uses: building understanding and building presentations. Distill, The Illustrated Transformer, and Transformer Explainer are explanatory tools aimed at comprehension. ML Visuals and Wikimedia Commons are supply libraries aimed at production of slides, papers, or other documents. The Transformer Explainer is the only item that runs live inference, putting a GPT-2 model in the browser with attention heads inspectable in real time, which makes it distinct in kind from the others.

The data covers transformer architecture heavily and does not extend to hardware photography, benchmark charts, or timelines beyond what the collection's own label promises. None of the five items directly addresses compute, power, or physical infrastructure. The connection to those topics would have to come from how these visual resources are used to teach the architectures that drive demand for compute, not from anything the items themselves contain.

The set is small at five entries and the verification date is uniform across all of them, so nothing here distinguishes items by recency or update frequency. Distill is explicitly archived, meaning its content is fixed.
